content.value_statement: Creating a complete plugin package requires manifests, components, templates, validation, and release planning. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through that workflow.
actual_capabilities: Designs plugin directory structures for agents, skills, commands, hooks, and support scripts.
Drafts plugin manifest fields and component registration paths.
Creates README, command, skill, agent, and hook templates for plugin packages.
Validates plugin metadata, component paths, README presence, and common safety issues.
Explains release, versioning, marketplace, and manual distribution workflows.
Documents security practices for tool permissions, secrets, scripts, and dependencies.
limitations: Does not publish plugins to a marketplace without user-controlled release steps.
Requires review before generated hooks or scripts run in a real project.
Cannot verify private marketplace rules unless the user provides them.
Template examples must be customized before production use.

use_cases.title: Create a New Plugin
use_cases.description: Generate a complete starter package with manifest, README, folders, and example components.
use_cases.target_user: Claude Code users building reusable tooling

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Automation
use_cases.description: Bundle shared agents, commands, hooks, and skills into one installable package.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Plugin Release
use_cases.description: Check structure, versioning, documentation, and distribution steps before publishing.
use_cases.target_user: Plugin authors preparing public or private releases

prompt_templates.title: Start a Plugin
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal Claude Code plugin named my-plugin with a manifest, README, and one example command.

prompt_templates.title: Add Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Add one agent, one skill, and one hook to this plugin. Keep paths valid and update the README.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Review an existing plugin before sharing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this plugin structure for manifest errors, missing files, unsafe scripts, and documentation gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a versioned release plan for this plugin, including migration notes, marketplace metadata, and security checks.

output_examples.input: Create a starter plugin for repository analysis.
output_examples.output: A plugin plan with required folders, manifest fields, README sections, and starter command, skill, and agent descriptions.
A validation report that lists missing metadata, weak documentation, component path issues, and recommended release fixes.
A hook design that explains the trigger, expected inputs, blocking behavior, and user review requirements.

best_practices: Keep plugin manifests simple, valid, and aligned with the actual component paths.
Review generated Bash hooks and scripts before enabling them in a project.
Document installation, configuration, security expectations, and release notes clearly.
anti_patterns: Do not bundle unrelated agents, commands, and skills into one vague plugin.
Do not hardcode real credentials, tokens, or private repository details in templates.
Do not publish generated hooks without testing their inputs and failure behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code plugin packages with manifests, components, templates, documentation, and validation guidance.

faq.question: Can it work with existing plugins?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review structure, update documentation, add components, and prepare release steps.

faq.question: Does it publish plugins automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains publishing steps, but users control repository, marketplace, and release actions.

faq.question: Does it require Bash access?
faq.answer: Some validation and hook examples use Bash. Users should review scripts before running them.

faq.question: Can it create plugin templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes minimal, standard, and full template patterns for common plugin layouts.

faq.question: Is it only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: It focuses on Claude Code plugin packaging, while marketplace metadata can reference Claude, Codex, and Claude Code discovery.
